summary:
The name of the bill is the "Passport (First Amendment) Bill, 2083" (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 1). The main purpose of this bill is to update the existing Passport Act, 2076 in a timely manner to address the latest standards of the International Civil Aviation Organization, clarify provisions regarding diplomatic, special, and temporary passports, make the passport distribution process service-oriented, clarify and simplify the procedures for cancelling, withholding, or non-issuance of passports, solve practical problems regarding temporary passports for minors abroad, and make penalties for passport misuse timely (Statement of Objects and Reasons). This Act shall come into force immediately (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

This bill defines foreign travel on official work as foreign travel undertaken for specified purposes such as participating in meetings, conferences, study, training, working in foreign missions, receiving medical treatment at government expense, or joining United Nations peace missions pursuant to the decision of the Federal Government, Provincial Government or subordinate body, Local Level, Federal Parliament, Provincial Assembly, or Constitutional Body (Section 2, Clause chha, Page 1). The Department shall issue a diplomatic passport based on a recommendation as per the decision of the Federal Parliament, Government of Nepal, Supreme Court, or Constitutional Body, or based on the recommendation of the concerned Ministry of the Government of Nepal upon nomination as per the decision of the Provincial Government or Local Level (Section 4, Clause a and b). Similarly, the Department shall issue a special passport based on a recommendation as per the decision of the Federal Parliament, Government of Nepal, Supreme Court, or Constitutional Body, or based on the recommendation of the concerned Ministry of the Government of Nepal upon nomination as per the decision of the Provincial Government or Local Level (Section 5, Clause a and b).

In the case of Nepalese citizens residing abroad, the Ministry may make arrangements to collect passport applications along with biometric details through the private sector or any other institution as prescribed (Section 6, Subsection 7, Page 3). If an application for a passport is submitted to an agency other than the Department, that agency shall, if it finds after inquiry that the passport can be issued, forward a recommendation to the Department for passport issuance (Section 6, Subsection 5, Page 3). An official or employee who has received a diplomatic or special passport shall return such passport to the Department within the prescribed period after the specified purpose ends or upon being relieved of office or suspended, provided that a person holding a specified public office may retain the diplomatic or special passport for the prescribed period (Section 11, Subsection 2, Page 6). Diplomatic or special passport holders going on official foreign travel may conduct personal travel for up to thirty days in addition to the travel itinerary before returning to Nepal, and employees working in a mission may conduct personal travel for up to ninety days after taking departure clearance from the mission before returning to Nepal (Section 11, Subsection 1, Clause b and c, Page 6). If the Department cannot issue a passport due to specified grounds, it must inform the concerned applicant within three days (Section 8, Subsection 3, Page 4). In cases where a passport is issued to a minor under special conditions, the minor's guardian must come to Nepal within the validity period of the issued passport and obtain a minor identity card or Nepalese citizenship certificate (Section 13, Subsection 2, Page 7).

This bill contains the following provisions regarding penalties. Obtaining a passport or travel document using a fake or forged citizenship certificate, national identity card, or minor identity card is punishable by a fine from Rs. 2 lakh to Rs. 5 lakh or imprisonment from 1 year to 3 years or both (Section 14, Clause a and Section 15, Subsection 1, Clause a, Page 8-9). Obtaining a passport using citizenship, national identity card, or minor identity card in another person's name or dual citizenship/ID is punishable by a fine from Rs. 2 lakh to Rs. 5 lakh or imprisonment from 1 year to 3 years or both (Section 14, Clause b and Section 15, Subsection 1, Clause a, Page 8-9). Allowing someone else to use one's passport or using another person's passport is punishable by a fine from Rs. 2 lakh to Rs. 5 lakh or imprisonment from 1 year to 3 years or both (Section 14, Clause c and Section 15, Subsection 1, Clause a, Page 8-9). Anyone other than an authorized official keeping control of another person's passport with mala fide intention without their consent is punishable by a fine from Rs. 2 lakh to Rs. 5 lakh or imprisonment from 1 year to 3 years or both (Section 14, Clause d and Section 15, Subsection 1, Clause a, Page 8-9). Obtaining a passport by altering the date of birth by more than one year is punishable by a fine of Rs. 10 thousand (Section 14, Clause e and Section 15, Subsection 1, Clause b, Page 8-9). Obtaining a passport by submitting false details is punishable by a fine from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 2 lakh (Section 14, Clause f and Section 15, Subsection 1, Clause c, Page 8-9). Using a passport for a purpose other than that for which it was issued is punishable by a fine from Rs. 2 lakh to Rs. 5 lakh or imprisonment from 1 year to 3 years or both (Section 14, Clause g and Section 15, Subsection 1, Clause a, Page 8-9). Anyone other than an authorized official altering details in a passport is punishable by a fine from Rs. 2 lakh to Rs. 5 lakh or imprisonment from 1 year to 3 years or both (Section 14, Clause h and Section 15, Subsection 1, Clause a, Page 9).
